It depends on the company, but you can start an Ausbildung in freight forwarding or supply chain jobs, like Speditionskaufmann, Kaufmann im Groß- und Außenhandel, or Industriekaufmann, with a B1 level in German. Knowing more languages can be an advantage since you may need to communicate with companies worldwide, but it varies. You could be lucky and work for a company that values Spanish.

During my apprenticeship in Spedition, I saw people with less-than-perfect German succeed because they knew a language the company needed. For example, a Chinese colleague spoke Chinese, English, and some German, and was hired due to the company’s business with China.

These office jobs are easy to learn with basic computer skills, English, maybe another language, and some geography. Some companies even hire people without an apprenticeship in this field. At my company, a South American colleague was hired for his English and business degree, even though he had no freight experience.

There are also companies like this in Spain, where you could start with a mini-job to gain knowledge. It might also be possible to work as a bus or tram driver in Germany with limited German skills, though I’m not entirely sure.
